title: DC Circuits
short_title: Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits and Kirchhoff's laws
standard_text: Electric circuits: charge, current, potential difference, resistance, Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits, Kirchhoff's laws, and electrical power and energy. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 11)
meta_desc: Free Physics 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits and Kirchhoff's laws. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Kirchhoff: current in = current out; voltages around a loop add to zero.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current I = Q ÷ t (amperes). Potential difference V is the energy per charge (volts). Ohm's law: V = IR. Power P = IV = I²R. Electrical energy E = Pt.

In series, Rtotal = R₁ + R₂ + …; in parallel, 1/Rtotal = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …. Kirchhoff's current law: the current into a junction equals the current out. Kirchhoff's voltage law: the potential rises and drops around any closed loop add to zero.

Example

Two 6 Ω resistors in parallel: total resistance?

1/R = 1/6 + 1/6

Answer: 3 Ω

Example

A 60 W bulb runs on 120 V. What current does it draw?

I = P ÷ V

Answer: 0.5 A

Common mistakes

  • Adding parallel resistances directly.
  • Thinking current is used up by a resistor.
  • Mixing up power and energy.

faq.q: Why does the total resistance drop when you add a parallel branch?
faq.a: The current has another path, so more total current flows.

faq.q: What is the internal resistance of a cell?
faq.a: The resistance inside the cell, which lowers the terminal voltage when current flows.
